reason: The cited evidence (E1) demonstrates that (CrFeTiTa)70W30 can be prepared by mechanical alloying and sintering and shows microstructural stability under Ar+, He+, and D+ irradiation, supporting the irradiation resistance premise. However, it provides no data on depositing this alloy as a thin interlayer at a W–Cu interface, nor on its effect on diffusion, interfacial coherence, void suppression, or thermal conductivity in a composite. Thus, most key premises specific to the intervention are unsupported.
premises: A (CrFeTiTa)70W30 HEA interlayer can be deposited as a thin, continuous film at the W–Cu interface.
The HEA interlayer establishes a graded, low-energy, coherent interphase that suppresses elemental diffusion.
The HEA interlayer possesses intrinsic irradiation resistance that stabilizes the microstructure under ion bombardment.
Suppressing diffusion and void formation via the interlayer enhances thermal conductivity relative to untreated W–Cu composites.
